title.en: Give parts stable identities before configuring them

summary: Model parts and options as data with stable identifiers, and treat meshes as one rendering of that data.
objective: Keep selection, compatibility and quantities correct when parts are swapped, hidden or duplicated.
applies_when: The user can swap variants, colours, sizes or optional modules.
Parts are counted, priced, labelled or checked for compatibility.
The same component appears several times in one assembly.
example_prompts: Let the user swap rig modules and show what stops fitting.
List the parts used in the current configuration.
negative_signals: Single fixed objects with no options and no part list.
Sculptural or organic forms that are not assembled from discrete components.
not_for: Single fixed objects with no options and no part list.
Sculptural or organic forms that are not assembled from discrete components.

principles: Mesh names are a rendering convenience. Once a part can be swapped, instanced or hidden, identity has to live in data that survives geometry changes.
Compatibility is a relation, not an appearance. Whether a module fits depends on declared interfaces, not on whether two meshes happen to touch.
Instances differ from types: four identical screws are one type and four placements, and confusing them corrupts both counting and selection.
Configuration is a state a viewer can reason about, so it should be inspectable and shareable rather than implied by which objects happen to be visible.
implementation: Define a part record with a stable identifier, a type, its interfaces and its placement, and build the scene graph from those records.
Express variant swaps as changing which type occupies a placement, keeping the placement identity, its labels and its selection state.
Declare interface compatibility explicitly and evaluate it in the model, then explain refusals in terms of the interface rather than silently disallowing a drag.
Derive counts, lists and prices from the records so the displayed bill of materials cannot drift from the visible configuration.
Keep hidden or filtered parts in the model as hidden, not deleted, so the configuration is not lost by a view operation.
observable_checks: Swap a variant and confirm the selection, labels and any measurement stay on the same placement.
Attempt an incompatible combination and confirm the refusal names the interface reason.
Compare the on-screen part count with the parts actually instantiated after several swaps and hides.
Reload from the stored configuration and confirm the scene matches what was exported.

creative_affordances: The interface vocabulary is yours to invent; a fictional product can have fictional mounts as long as they are declared.
Presentation of compatibility can be playful, from a snap-fit animation to a colour-coded mount, provided the model decides the result.
known_limits: Authored data-modelling guidance; no runtime configurator has been exercised for this record.
It does not model manufacturing tolerances, real supplier catalogues or pricing rules.
